page.notes: Long s is printed as a sign like s and is transcribed as plain s throughout. "Deniq;" and "Atq;" use a superscript sign after q that is not clearly legible; copied as q; with the sign read as a standard abbreviation, so check against the scan. The Greek words in the fifth paragraph are rendered from a small, blurred print: the first ([?]βαλητὸν) and the accents are uncertain, and so are the words καθ' ἀλήθειαν and κατὰ δόξαν. The word after "Ha-" at the line end ("befis") is doubtful; read as "besis" with [?]. In the last line, "Ad" stands on the same line as the text and is read as text, not as a catchword. Two of the line-end hyphens ("phy-", "elige-") were preserved as printed. The margin notes "II." and "III." are roman numerals beside the notes and are kept inside them.
